sources.entry: AURA Switcher - Fixes text typed in the wrong keyboard layout right after Space; double Shift converts the last word. A Punto Switcher alternative.

summary.one_liner: A menu-bar app for macOS and Windows that fixes text typed in the wrong keyboard layout (e.g. "ghbdsn" → "привіт") and converts text with a double Shift tap.
keywords: fix text typed in wrong language
summary.what_it_does: AURA Switcher runs in the menu bar (macOS) or system tray (Windows) and starts at login. When you type a word in the wrong layout and press Space, it erases the word, retypes it in the correct layout, and switches the layout; word checking uses the system spell checker. Double-tapping Shift converts selected text to the next layout, or the last typed word if nothing is selected, or just switches the layout. Users can set app exclusions, per-app layout bindings, word exceptions, and automatic pausing in games. The README says AURA uses every layout enabled in macOS and that Windows support is in beta, with a separate C++ build. Updates are checked only when the user opens the check page in the browser, since the app itself makes no network requests.
use_cases: fix text typed in the wrong keyboard layout
switch between Ukrainian, Russian and English typing
convert selected text to another layout
keep a keyboard layout per application
correct slang or custom words with exceptions
how_to_run: Grant access: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility → enable AURA Switcher
Windows: download AURA-Switcher-windows-x64.zip from the release and run AURA Switcher.exe (no installer)
Build Windows version on a Mac: windows/build.sh (needs Zig)
notable: Listen-only CGEventTap, so it cannot freeze keyboard or mouse input
Character tables are built from the macOS layouts themselves, so any installed layout works without manual setup
Windows build is a single C++/Win32 file with no installer; ARM64 build listed as untested
Makes no network requests; update check is a browser page opened on demand
caveats: macOS 13+ and Windows 10/11 only; iPhone/iPad/Android only as a separate keyboard with little practical value
Windows support is beta, tested on x64 only; ARM64 not yet tested; SmartScreen warns about unknown publisher; cannot see keystrokes in administrator apps
Auto-correction only sees continuous typing; mouse clicks, arrow keys or ⌘/⌥/⌃ shortcuts reset the current word; password fields and some apps may behave differently
Chinese and Japanese input not supported; auto-correction skipped between similar Latin layouts (EN/DE/FR)
